reduceIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE below $64,110, which is the UTC daily EMA20 at 64,113.34. That line has now held on a closing basis for four consecutive UTC days and is the floor of the entire reclaim thesis. The 4H EMA20 at 64,060.89 sits 50 points beneath it and the 346.87K CoinGlass pool at 64,052.84 sits just under that, so losing 64,110 on a close does not stop at 64,110 - it opens a 60-point air pocket into a measured liquidation shelf, and beneath that the single largest object on the entire surface, the 1.09M pool at 63,842.12. Note the trigger has travelled UP again, from the midday's 64,050, because the daily EMA20 has risen with the market. The intermediate warnings between spot and it are the 1h EMA20 at 64,517.84 and the 1h EMA50 at 64,202.40.

addIf.confirmation: A 4H CLOSE above $65,110, which is the price of the 909.98K CoinGlass magnet at 65,106.44 - the heaviest single object anywhere above spot and the reason both attempts at the 65,000 handle today were sold. Price tagged 65,026.6 at 16:15 COT and could not close a 4H bar above it; the 20:00-00:00 UTC bar closed at 64,659.3. A genuine break has to eat that 909.98K and then the 490.92K at 65,457.64 before the 65,423.7 swing high from 31 Jul is in play. Anything less than a 4H close is another wick into a wall that has already rejected twice.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from the midday's ADD to REDUCE, and the reason is the calendar rather than a change of view. The directional read is unchanged and still bullish: the 4H stack is fully ordered with price above EMA20/50/100/200, the daily EMA20 and EMA50 are both reclaimed, and the day closed +0.94% on the UTC session. What changed is that the next report is roughly thirteen hours away, the wallet is 98% invested with 3.79 USDT of cash, and the largest measured liquidity pool on the board sits 852 points below spot with nothing but a 346.87K shelf in between. A 10% spot trim is not a bearish call - it is buying back the dry powder needed to hit 63,842 if the overnight gap delivers it. The stop recommendation is NEW this session: it was false at midday and is true now.

overnightRisk: The gap window runs from now (19:45 COT) to roughly 02:00 COT, and three specific things can move it. ONE, the liquidity geometry is asymmetric in size but not in distance. Above spot sits 909.98K at 65,106.44, only 412 points away or 0.27 of a daily ATR - close enough that a thin-book Asian bid can reach it. Below sits 346.87K at 64,052.84 and then 1.09M at 63,842.12, the biggest object anywhere on the 48-hour surface, 852 points down or 0.56 ATR. Proximity favours a squeeze up; magnitude favours a flush down. That is a genuinely two-sided overnight, and it is why the answer is a resting stop rather than a directional bet. TWO, the 05 Aug Farside row is INCOMPLETE - it prints +47.6M but the IBIT column is still a dash, so the number that carried this move (+170.1M on 03 Aug, +211.5M on 04 Aug) has not been confirmed for today. If IBIT lands negative when the row completes overnight, the three-day inflow streak that underwrote the reclaim breaks, and the 64,110 line is the first thing that gets tested. THREE, sentiment is the odd man out: the Fear & Greed Index reads 25, Extreme Fear, on a day price closed up 0.94% and above both the daily EMA20 and EMA50. Extreme Fear into a rising tape is usually fuel, but it also means positioning is light and conviction is thin, so overnight moves in either direction will travel further per unit of flow than they should. Add the mechanical detail that the OKX 8-hour funding just settled at +0.0068% and the current period reads +0.0078% - fractionally positive, longs paying, but nowhere near the crowding that capped the last two attempts. The single most likely bad outcome is a 63,842 tag on thin Asian liquidity that reverses by morning; the stop at 64,020 sits above that pool deliberately, so it protects the trim without donating the core to the magnet.

It is close enough to be reachable on thin overnight liquidity and heavy enough that clearing it on a 4H close would be a real signal rather than a wick.

It sits 641.3 points below spot and, importantly, immediately beneath the cluster of moving averages that define the reduce trigger - the daily EMA20 at 64,113.34 and the 4H EMA20 at 64,060.89. That stacking is why a close below 64,110 is dangerous rather than merely uncomfortable: the first thing under the line is a liquidation shelf, not support.

It sits 852 points beneath spot, 0.56 of a daily ATR, and it is the same pool the midday session measured at 63,749.44; it has drifted UP roughly 93 points as leverage rebuilt with the market. It also sits 38.6 points under today's UTC low of 63,880.7, which means a break of the day's low runs straight into it. This is the destination if the overnight bid fails, and it is exactly why the recommended stop is placed at 64,020 - above the pool, not inside it.

liquidityMagnet.note: Deliberately called BALANCED rather than up or down, because the two readings disagree and saying so is more useful than picking one. By SIZE the pull is down: 1.09M at 63,842.12 outweighs 909.98K at 65,106.44. By DISTANCE the pull is up: the 909.98K sits 412 points away versus 852 points to the 1.09M, so a distance-weighted score reads 2.21 above against 1.28 below. Positioning does not break the tie either - the CoinGlass 24h long/short split is 49.75/50.25, a ratio of 0.99, which is as close to neutral as this metric gets and means neither side is crowded enough to be the fuel. The honest conclusion is that the overnight is genuinely two-sided and the correct expression of that is a resting stop rather than a directional add.

calibration.rollingRecord: The midday call scored well on level and poorly on follow-through. Its 64,050 reduce level was never approached - the afternoon low of 64,568.2 held 518 points clear of it, so the decision not to recommend a resting stop was correct for the window it covered. Its 64,700 4H-close add trigger was TAGGED but never confirmed: price reached 65,026.6 at 16:15 COT, but no 4H bar closed above 65,270, the level the midday report actually required for its add. The bullish direction did not pay from the midday mark - price is 84.1 points lower at 64,694.1, so actingHelped is false rather than true. The 3.5 USDT tranche the midday session deployed at 64,778.2 is underwater by 0.13%, about 0.005 USDT, which is noise but is still the wrong sign. Across the day the wallet is up: the morning's 15 USDT at 64,526.4 is +0.26%, and the daily-EMA20 reclaim thesis that has run since the midnight session is intact.
calibration.note: One correction to carry forward and one thing the midday session got right that deserves recording. THE CORRECTION: the midday report set its add trigger at a 4H close above 65,270 to clear the whole resistance shelf, then also wrote 64,700 into the operational language inherited from the morning. Two numbers for one trigger is how a session ends up claiming a tag it did not earn. This session states one trigger, 65,110, and it is the price of the measured 909.98K magnet - not a round number and not a shelf midpoint. THE THING IT GOT RIGHT: the midday session refused to open a leveraged long 284 points beneath a measured 450K shelf. Price ran 248 points further and then gave all of it back, so a futures leg would have been stopped or scratched for nothing. The lesson generalises - when the nearest measured magnet is inside half an ATR, leverage is paying for a move the book has already priced.
